page: UpCloud STARTER-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared x86_64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 4 physical cores and single-thread-per-core execution. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and a bundled 50 GB local SSD. The server also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a mixture of performance tiers. Single-core CPU performance is strong, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2758.58, placing it in the top 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression reaching 33.57 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations lean average to weak. The stress-ng multi-core score is 9375.63, which is in the middle 50%, while the Passmark memory score and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Notably, large-block read-only memory bandwidth is poor at 6.32 GB/sec, indicating potential bottlenecks during large-dataset memory transfers.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation and starter tier classification position this server as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU resources. The balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio is suitable for general-purpose workloads. Appropriate use cases include static web serving, Redis caching, basic software compilation, and lightweight text or image processing, whereas memory-intensive databases or heavy multi-threaded compute tasks may encounter performance limitations due to the shared CPU model and lower memory bandwidth.
